person_note: The controlling narrator is Diana, who narrates as a participating “I.” Numerous event passages independently expose that voice across immediate scenes, memories, pandemic experiences, family relationships, and the later three-year retrospective, so the quote evidence is not confined to isolated speech or an embedded document. The authorized author and publisher excerpts corroborate the first-person opening, while the whole-book study guide identifies Diana as primary and explains that Finn contributes only sporadic first-person emails in Part 1. Those emails add another first-person voice but do not create alternation between grammatical persons; under the methodology, multiple first-person narrators remain FIRST. Generic “you” aphorisms, dialogue, and bare third-person speech beats are local or nondiagnostic. No credible contrary evidence was found.
